summary: Total cholesterol adds together the cholesterol carried in all lipoprotein particles. It is a blunt number on its own, because it cannot tell a high protective HDL from a high harmful LDL.
what_it_measures: The total concentration of cholesterol in blood across all lipoprotein fractions, reported in mmol/L.

reference_ranges.note: UK target for the general population

interpretations.meaning: A raised total cholesterol needs breaking down into its parts before it means anything. A high value driven by HDL carries a very different implication from the same value driven by LDL.
typical_next_steps: full lipid profile including HDL and LDL

when_to_seek_help: Do not act on total cholesterol alone. Ask for the breakdown, and discuss your overall cardiovascular risk with your GP.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
